stage_1.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Corporate Extract of the foreign investing corporation (e.g., Chinese parent, if the LP investor is corporate)
stage_1.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / Chinese business registry; or equivalent Companies House
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarization by a Chinese notary, then apostille by the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs/authorized provincial Foreign Affairs Office (China acceded to the Apostille Convention on 7 Nov 2023); no consular legalization by the Consulate General of Canada is required; apostilled document then certified translation into English/BC Registry-ready form

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 349, ss. 3-8 (registration and governance); Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348 (general partner duties); Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (if a corporate general partner is used).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, operated by the Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia, acting for the Registrar of Companies, Victoria, BC.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP - Statement of Registration of a Limited Partnership under the Limited Partnership Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None by statute; partner contributions are contractual and set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement. No escrow account or minimum bank balance is required. A registered office in British Columbia and, if no BC-resident general partner, a BC attorney for service are mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the General Partner of [●] Limited Partnership adopts this First Resolution on the date first written above; that the contributions, profit/loss percentages and capital subscription details stated in the registered Statement of Registration and Limited Partnership Agreement are ratified; that the registered office at [● street address], British Columbia, and the designated representative for service are approved; that the General Partner is empowered to open and operate banking accounts, execute aviation and catering contracts, and engage the initial registered agent, auditor, and counsel; that the fiscal year-end is [date]; and that officers/attorneys appointed herein may attest documents and file registrations. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and general partner consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services - Name Reconciliation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed limited partnership names through bcregistry.ca; verify uniqueness in the BC Corporate Registry; obtain executed consents from each general partner; confirm the registered office street address and attorney for service in BC.
required_dossiers: Consent of attorney for service (if non-resident general partner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused, resubmit alternate names within the 28-day reservation window; a priority resubmission can be requested by phone. No material filing fee penalty applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a Limited Partnership Agreement governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distributions, management authority, indemnities, and withdrawal rights; obtain e-signatures and notarize signatures of non-resident partners; collect know-your-partner records for bank and tax filing purposes.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for foreign general partner (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incomplete signature pages are cured by executing and delivering an amending schedule; foreign signatures require an apostille to be accepted in BC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Form LP and pay registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Online Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP online and upload the executed Statement of Registration; verify the LP name, BC registered office, full legal names of all general partners, attorney for service, and contribution summary; pay the filing fee by card; download the Notice of Registration once the registrar issues it.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical rejections are cured by refiling a corrected Form LP within 15 days without judicial application; expedited processing is available for time-sensitive transactions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA and BC tax account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use CRA Business Registration Online to obtain a Business Number with GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts as applicable; open a WorkSafeBC account; register for BC PST if taxable food or beverage sales occur; register for BC Employer Health Tax if payroll exceeds the BC threshold.
required_dossiers: Notice of Registration from BC Registries
General partner identification and Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA program-access queries are resolved by amending the application in My Business Account or calling CRA Business Enquiries; corrections made within 30 days avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance records and bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner, registered office, and commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first general partner resolution; adopt the registered office and representative for service; open a commercial bank account using the Notice of Registration and resolution; establish the limited partnership minute book and register of partners; file any consequential declarations under the Limited Partnership Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Omitted records are remedied by filing post-formation consents and declarations; bank KYC resubmission is accepted within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: British Columbia Ministry of Health (Environmental Health), applicable regional health authority (Vancouver Coastal Health or Fraser Health), Technical Safety BC, and Vancouver Airport Authority for ramp access and airside security.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Premises Operating Permit / Food Service Establishment Permit issued by the regional health authority; Airport Restricted Area Identification Card (RAIC) and Aviation Catering Ramp Access Permit issued by the airport authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Environmental Assessment Office with Metro Vancouver Regional District (Environmental Regulation and Enforcement Division)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Assessment Act review for a catering kitchen; subject to regional food-processing discharge registration and a municipal/business licensing inspection.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Metro Vancouver Sewer Use Bylaw No. 299: BOD less than or equal to 300 mg/L, TSS less than or equal to 300 mg/L, oil and grease less than or equal to 50 mg/L, pH 5.5-11.0; grease interceptors required at cook-line and scullery drains; kitchen exhaust and fire suppression compliant with NFPA 96 and BC Fire Code; refrigerants managed in accordance with the BC Ozone-Depleting Substances Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and inspection clearance; BC Fire Code fire safety certificate from the local authority having jurisdiction; Technical Safety BC permits for gas, refrigeration, and mechanical systems; structural load certification for food-processing and baking equipment; airport security clearance for all catering staff performing direct ramp delivery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary and financial-system supervisor; the Minister of Finance has statutory authority over currency and exchange-rate policy; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) regulates federally authorized banks; FINTRAC administers AML/CFT and electronic funds transfer reporting. Canada has no separate foreign exchange control administration and does not require government approval for cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility of the Canadian dollar for both current-account and capital-account transactions, consistent with its obligations under IMF Article VIII. There are no exchange controls, no non-resident account restrictions, no multiple currency practices, and no impediments to profit remittance or capital repatriation by a BC limited partnership. A non-resident limited partner is subject to Canadian income tax and withholding only to the extent distributions represent Canadian-source taxable income under the Income Tax Act, Part XIII, with treaty relief available under applicable tax treaties. The partnership must ensure that distributions to non-resident partners are properly characterized and that all required information returns and withholdings are filed. Banks and payment intermediaries must aggregate and report electronic funds transfers of CA$10,000 or more to FINTRAC and maintain records sufficient to meet CDR/AML obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no time-limited repatriation period, and no domiciliary holding requirement for export earnings. Export receipts may be held in foreign currency accounts at Canadian Schedule I banks or converted at negotiated market rates. The only applicable compliance duties are standard FINTRAC reporting for EFTs at or above CA$10,000, retention of underlying trade documentation, and, where applicable, Customs Act export declarations for physical goods leaving Canada. Airline inflight catering kitchen revenues generated from sales outside Canada therefore may be received and retained in USD or CAD as commercial prudence dictates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury rail; Medium as an auxiliary cross-border payment channel if the provider is a FINTRAC-registered Money Services Business and, where applicable, registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act supervision. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business or Revolut cannot replace a Canadian Schedule I bank for the limited partnership because the EMI may not lawfully accept deposits or operate as an authorized foreign bank in Canada. An unregistered offshore EMI holding funds for a BC-resident partnership could create AML, anti-money-laundering, and insolvency risk. The EMI channel may be used only for low-value vendor payments with the ultimate settlement always sweeping into a domestic bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or live-video banking-counsel KYC/CDD interview is mandatory for initial onboarding of the BC limited partnership. Canadian chartered banks will not complete a fully remote opening for a non-resident-controlled LP. The standard market practice is an in-person visit by the authorized general partner representative at a Vancouver business banking centre, or a high-definition video interview with notarized and apostilled corporate documents. The corporate general partner must produce a board resolution designating the authorized signatory; non-resident directors are not required to attend personally if a properly appointed Canadian-resident signatory or attorney-in-fact appears in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to establish the economic substance of the LP, including no active operations, no physical BC kitchen premises, and reliance on unidentified offshore investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: certified BC Limited Partnership registration certificate; complete limited partnership agreement; general partner appointment resolution; register of partners with percentages of ownership; ultimate beneficial ownership table (name, residence, nationality, tax identification number); lease or ownership proof of the catering kitchen site; executed or draft airline caterer agreements; and a board-approved cash-flow and capital contribution schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border transaction volume disproportionate to contributed capital, with rapid inbound-outbound movement and interposed payment chains involving third-country correspondents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: audited or reviewed financial statements; bank reference letter from the originating foreign bank; underlying supply and off take contracts (airline meal orders, raw-food purchase orders); invoices with full goods descriptions; capital call notices; source of wealth and source of funds statement; and an organizational chart showing all intermediaries and final beneficiaries for bank matching.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign general partner or affiliate injecting large capital via short-term loans causing an ambiguous debt-versus-equity structure or potential disguised deposit risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: executed and dated loan or capital contribution agreements; capital call notices and payment instructions; bank statements showing the sourcing account from which funds originated; partner tax identification numbers and CRS self-certifications; an arm's length interest analysis and tax legal opinion; and a commitment that repayments will be made only to the original originating bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or politically exposed person (PEP) detection on any limited partner, director, general partner entity, or ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: enhanced due diligence questionnaire; comprehensive curriculum vitae for each individual; sanctions and PEP screening reports with false-positive resolution narratives; notarized government-issued identification; source of wealth documentation (provenance of funds through salaries, dividends, or sale of assets); professional reference letters from a bank or regulated law firm; and evidence that the LP relationship is subject to continuous quarterly re-screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing uses SWIFT MT103 (direct) or MT202 (correspondent cover) from the foreign partner's bank to the BC LP's account at a Canadian Schedule I clearing member. Beneficiary legal name must match exactly the BC Registry registered name; the remittance information field must distinctly state 'CA_LP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION [capital call reference]' or 'NON-RESIDENT PARTNER LOAN [agreement reference]'. The Canadian bank will require the underlying capital call or loan agreement for AML clearance. Although Canada imposes no foreign exchange permission, FINTRAC reporting applies to all electronic funds transfers of CA$10,000 or more; splitting a wire to circumvent thresholds is illegal. For USD investment, the LP may maintain an USD account, or conversion to CAD may be executed as a spot transaction with prior order and the same bank to preserve audit traceability. Tax identification numbers and Canadian residency status of each contributing partner must be disclosed to satisfy CRS and beneficial ownership verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and trade settlement clearing rails are as follows: (a) vendor wires via SWIFT MT103 with invoice references; (b) payroll and recurring domestic supplier payments via ACSS EFT/ACH in CAD; (c) USD-denominated monthly airline contract settlements via ACH through the bank's US Federal Reserve clearing channel; and (d) cross-border bulk ingredients and aviation supply purchases via documentary commercial letters of credit (MT700 issued by the Canadian bank under UCP600) with the beneficiary's advising bank where the trade amount and credit risk justify LC terms. All outbound transfers must carry the corresponding invoice or contract number in the remittance field, be backed by purchase orders, customs declarations for physical imports where applicable, and FINTRAC reporting if over CA$10,000. For USD supplier payments, the LP should pre-fund the USD account via CAD/USD spot or forward rather than issuing multiple ad-hoc conversions to maintain a clear taxable and treasury trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable USD/CAD forward contract (corporately master-agreed with non-leveraged margin)
USD/CAD FX swap or rollover swap for periodic rolling of near-dated forward exposures
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on permitted non-CAD currencies where the receiving jurisdiction imposes delivery restrictions (e.g., certain emerging-market trade counterparties)
Cross-currency swap (USD/CAD) under an ISDA Master Agreement for multi-year aviation contract asset/liability matching
European-style vanilla FX option (USD/CAD put or call) used to cap conversion cost while preserving upside

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the anniversary of the limited partnership registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to $500 CAD and risk of administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general mandatory audit requirement for private limited partnerships; independent audit may be triggered by specific revenue thresholds, public company status, or partnership agreement provisions

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation and update of ultimate beneficial ownership and partner details, including any changes from shareholding transfers or control modifications

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-1000 USD depending on entity size and requirements

stage_6.entry_description: Gross sales and services revenue: total invoiced airline inflight catering contracts, including ancillary bonded stores, net of returns and allowances.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source revenue if any non-resident partner relies on treaty relief; allocate revenue to the Canadian PE. Include exempt international inbound service revenue only to the extent attributable to the Canadian kitchen.
